source_refs.note: Topic 1.6, printed pages 6-7: deducing configuration from period, block and group, with Quick Check 1.2 as the self-check.

blocks.text: The periodic arrangement of the elements offers valuable insight into their physical properties, such as physical state and atomic radius, and into their electronic structure and chemical reactivity.

items: The period number is the principal quantum number n, the number of electron shells around the nucleus. An element X in the third period has three shells, with its valence electrons in the third. The subshell that holds them depends on the element's block (the azimuthal quantum number): if X in period 3 is in the s block, its valence electrons are in the 3s subshell.

The group number indicates the number of valence electrons. An element in period 3 and group 2 has two valence electrons in its outermost shell, so an element in period 3, group 2 (s block) has two electrons in the 3s subshell and must be magnesium (Mg).

blocks.text: Another example relates period and group number to configuration and position. If X belongs to group 13 and period 3, it has three valence electrons (group 13) in the third shell (period 3), so its configuration is 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p1, with the first, second and third shells filled in that order. Understanding the periodic arrangement therefore explains an element's electronic configuration, which is essential for understanding its chemical properties and behaviour.
